_source_note: Draft v0. Properties (rasa/virya/vipaka/dosha_effects) are drawn from widely corroborated traditional Ayurvedic knowledge cross-referenced across multiple secondary sources, NOT a verbatim extraction from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu or any single copyrighted text. Nutritional macros (calories/protein/carbs/fat) are approximate, typical values per 100g and should be verified against IFCT 2017 (Indian Food Composition Tables) or USDA FoodData Central before production use. Entries marked 'contested: true' have real disagreement across different classical/regional traditions - flagged in 'notes'. THIS ENTIRE FILE REQUIRES REVIEW AND CORRECTION BY A QUALIFIED AYURVEDIC PRACTITIONER BEFORE USE IN ANY PATIENT-FACING FEATURE.

foods.name: Basmati Rice (white, cooked)
foods.notes: Generally the most agreeable grain across all doshas in moderate quantity; excess may increase Kapha.

foods.name: Moong Dal (split green gram, cooked)
foods.notes: Considered tridoshic (balances all three doshas); the most recommended legume in Ayurvedic dietetics, especially when well-cooked with digestive spices.

foods.name: Cow's Ghee (clarified butter)
foods.notes: Highly valued in classical texts as a vehicle (anupana) for herbs and for nourishing tissues (dhatus); moderation matters more than avoidance.

foods.name: Ginger (fresh)
contraindications: high Pitta / acidity in excess quantity
foods.notes: Classic digestive aid (deepana-pachana); excellent for Vata and Kapha, use moderately for Pitta constitutions.

foods.name: Turmeric (fresh/powder)
foods.notes: Widely used for its anti-inflammatory and blood-purifying (raktashodhaka) action; generally well tolerated by all doshas in food quantities.

foods.name: Cumin Seeds
foods.notes: Core digestive spice (deepana); mild on Pitta compared to other heating spices.

foods.name: Black Pepper
foods.notes: One of the three components of Trikatu; strongly kindles agni (digestive fire).

foods.name: Green Cardamom
foods.notes: Tridoshic; commonly used to balance heavier or heating foods (e.g. added to milk, coffee, sweets).

foods.name: Cow's Milk (whole, warm)
foods.notes: Best taken warm, alone (not combined with sour, salty, or fish per viruddha ahara guidance), ideally at night for Vata/Pitta types.

foods.name: Yogurt / Curd
foods.notes: Traditionally avoided in the evening/night and in combination with fruit; best consumed fresh, at room temperature, in daytime.

foods.name: Buttermilk (takra, diluted, spiced)
foods.notes: Classically considered a digestive aid unlike plain yogurt, especially when spiced with cumin; better tolerated by Pitta than yogurt.

foods.name: Honey (raw, unheated)
contraindications: NEVER heat/cook honey - classical texts consider heated honey to produce ama (toxins)
foods.notes: Unique among sweet-tasting substances for reducing Kapha; the 'never heat honey' rule is a specific, frequently repeated classical guideline.

foods.name: Jaggery (unrefined cane sugar)
foods.notes: Preferred over refined white sugar in Ayurvedic dietetics for its mineral content, but still a concentrated sweet best used moderately.

foods.name: Whole Wheat
foods.notes: Good for Vata and Pitta; Kapha types generally do better favoring lighter grains like barley or millet.

foods.name: Barley
foods.notes: One of the best grains for Kapha and for weight management; needs adequate oiliness/warmth in preparation to suit Vata types.

foods.name: Spinach
contraindications: kidney stones (oxalate content) - use with caution
foods.notes: Best cooked with a little fat/ghee for Vata types to offset its light, dry quality.

foods.name: Bitter Gourd (karela)
contraindications: hypoglycemia/on diabetes medication - can lower blood sugar further
foods.notes: Some sources classify its virya as cooling rather than heating - traditions vary; well-documented as a blood sugar-lowering, Kapha-Pitta balancing vegetable regardless.

foods.name: Bottle Gourd (lauki)
foods.notes: Considered one of the most agreeable, easily digestible vegetables across all constitutions, especially favorable for Pitta.

foods.name: Coconut (fresh)
foods.notes: One of the best cooling foods for Pitta; Kapha types should moderate quantity.

foods.name: Banana (ripe)
contraindications: should not be combined with milk per viruddha ahara - considered incompatible
foods.notes: Heavy, nourishing, good for Vata and Pitta; Kapha types and those with congestion should limit.

foods.name: Apple
foods.notes: Raw apple can be slightly aggravating for Vata due to its light, dry quality; stewed/cooked apple is traditionally preferred for Vata types.

foods.name: Mango (ripe)
foods.notes: Virya classification varies across sources - some texts consider ripe mango cooling in moderate quantity despite general heating tendency; moderation is the consistent guidance regardless.

foods.name: Lemon
contraindications: active acid reflux/high Pitta in excess
foods.notes: Commonly used to kindle digestion; good for Vata and Kapha, use moderately for Pitta.

foods.name: Garlic (raw)
contraindications: traditionally avoided by some spiritual/sattvic diet practitioners
foods.notes: Potent rasayana (rejuvenative) for Vata and Kapha in classical use; use cautiously for Pitta-dominant individuals.

foods.name: Onion (raw)
foods.notes: Cooked onion is generally milder on Pitta than raw; good for Vata and Kapha types.

foods.name: Almonds (soaked, peeled)
foods.notes: Soaking and peeling (removing the skin) is a classical preparation specifically to make almonds lighter and more suitable for Pitta and Kapha types.

foods.name: Sesame Oil
foods.notes: The primary oil used in classical Ayurvedic external therapies (abhyanga) for Vata; internally best suited for Vata constitutions.

foods.name: Coriander (fresh leaves)
foods.notes: One of the few cooling, digestion-supporting herbs; particularly favorable for Pitta, tridoshic overall.

foods.name: Fenugreek Seeds (methi)
contraindications: pregnancy - traditionally used cautiously in large/medicinal doses
foods.notes: Commonly used for Vata and Kapha imbalances, particularly for digestion and blood sugar support; moderate for Pitta.

foods.name: Tomato (raw)
contraindications: inflammatory joint conditions - some traditions advise limiting nightshades
foods.notes: Nightshade family; a number of Ayurvedic practitioners advise limiting tomatoes for Pitta-dominant or Vata-Pitta imbalance individuals and in inflammatory joint conditions, though this is not universally agreed and is more a modern clinical-Ayurvedic recommendation than a strict classical one.

foods.name: Chana Dal (split chickpea, cooked)
foods.notes: Like most dals other than moong, benefits from being well-cooked and spiced (cumin, asafoetida) to offset its Vata-aggravating tendency.

foods.name: Toor Dal / Arhar Dal (pigeon pea, cooked)
foods.notes: One of the most commonly used dals in Indian cooking; moderate Vata-aggravating tendency, milder than rajma or chana.

foods.name: Urad Dal (black gram, cooked)
foods.notes: Unlike most legumes, urad is heavy and unctuous rather than light and dry - specifically favored for Vata disorders and used in classical strength-building (rasayana) preparations, but should be limited by Kapha and Pitta types.

foods.name: Masoor Dal (red lentil, cooked)
foods.notes: Easier to digest than chana or rajma; a reasonable middle-ground dal choice.

foods.name: Rajma (kidney beans, cooked)
foods.notes: Among the more Vata-aggravating legumes; best balanced with digestive spices (cumin, ajwain, hing) and adequate cooking.

foods.name: Ragi / Finger Millet
foods.notes: Calcium-rich millet, favored in modern Ayurvedic clinical practice for Kapha types and diabetic diets; needs oil/ghee to balance for Vata types.

foods.name: Bajra / Pearl Millet
foods.notes: Traditionally eaten in winter for its heating quality; good for Kapha, best avoided or limited in hot weather or by Pitta-dominant individuals.

foods.name: Jowar / Sorghum
foods.notes: Similar profile to ragi - good for Kapha and weight management, needs adequate oiliness for Vata types.

foods.name: Oats (rolled, dry)
foods.notes: Not part of the classical Ayurvedic corpus (a Western grain with minimal classical textual reference) - this classification is a modern clinical Ayurvedic extrapolation based on its similarity to barley, not a traditional source.

foods.name: Poha (flattened rice, dry)
foods.notes: Shares rice's cooling, light quality; commonly prepared with oil/tempering which changes its effective guna toward heavier and more Kapha-increasing.

foods.name: Paneer (fresh cottage cheese, unsalted)
foods.notes: Shares milk's general properties; nourishing for Vata and Pitta, best in moderation for Kapha.

foods.name: Carrot (cooked)
foods.notes: Raw carrot is slightly more Vata-aggravating than cooked; cooking (with a little ghee/oil) makes it more Vata-friendly.

foods.name: Beetroot (cooked)
foods.notes: Good blood-building (raktavardhaka) vegetable in classical/clinical use; moderate for Pitta due to its heating quality.

foods.name: Pumpkin
foods.notes: Well tolerated across constitutions, particularly favorable for Pitta.

foods.name: Cauliflower
contraindications: gas/bloating-prone or high-Vata individuals should limit raw preparations
foods.notes: Cruciferous vegetables as a class are well documented (both classically and in modern clinical Ayurveda) as gas-forming and Vata-aggravating, especially raw; cooking with digestive spices reduces this effect.

foods.name: Cabbage
contraindications: gas/bloating-prone or high-Vata individuals should limit raw preparations
foods.notes: Same cruciferous-family caution as cauliflower.

foods.name: Potato (boiled)
foods.notes: New World crop, introduced to India after the 1500s - NOT present in the classical Nighantu corpus (Bhavaprakasha Nighantu predates its introduction). This classification reflects modern clinical Ayurvedic practice, where potato (especially fried) is commonly considered heavy, dry, and Vata-aggravating and not particularly nourishing.

foods.name: Sweet Potato (boiled)
foods.notes: Also a New World crop, not present in classical texts; modern clinical Ayurveda generally considers it more nourishing and less Vata-aggravating than regular potato.

foods.name: Okra / Bhindi
foods.notes: Its mucilaginous quality is traditionally considered soothing, making it more Vata-friendly than most light, dry vegetables.

foods.name: Cucumber
foods.notes: One of the best cooling foods for Pitta, especially in hot weather; high water content can increase Kapha in excess.

foods.name: Green Peas
foods.notes: Legume-family gas-forming tendency similar to dals; moderate for Vata types.

foods.name: Grapes
foods.notes: Classically praised, especially black/dark grapes, as one of the most tridoshic-friendly fruits for Vata-Pitta constitutions.

foods.name: Orange
foods.notes: Citrus fruits generally heating; good for Vata and Kapha, moderate for Pitta.

foods.name: Papaya (ripe)
contraindications: pregnancy - unripe/semi-ripe papaya traditionally avoided due to uterine-stimulant properties
foods.notes: New World crop, introduced to India post-1500s, not present in the classical Nighantu corpus. Well known modern digestive aid (papain enzyme); some sources classify its Pitta effect as neutral rather than increasing - moderate disagreement across modern clinical sources.

foods.name: Pomegranate
foods.notes: Classically praised as tridoshic and heart-healthy (hridya); one of the most universally well-tolerated fruits across constitutions.

foods.name: Watermelon
contraindications: traditionally advised to be eaten alone, not combined with other foods (viruddha ahara guidance applying broadly to melons)
foods.notes: Excellent for Pitta and summer heat; its cold, watery quality is traditionally considered best eaten on its own away from other meals.

foods.name: Dates (dried)
contraindications: diabetes - use with caution due to high sugar concentration
foods.notes: Classic rasayana (rejuvenative, strength-building) food, especially valued for Vata and for weight/strength gain.

foods.name: Fennel Seeds (saunf)
foods.notes: Unusual among digestive spices for being cooling rather than heating; classic after-meal digestive, well tolerated by Pitta unlike most other spices.

foods.name: Ajwain / Carom Seeds
foods.notes: Strong classical digestive used for bloating and gas relief; traditionally recommended postpartum for Vata pacification.

foods.name: Asafoetida (hing)
contraindications: use only in small pinches - potent
foods.notes: One of the most classically praised digestive aids specifically for Vata-related gas and bloating; classically paired with legumes (dal) to offset their Vata-aggravating quality - a well-established, widely used combination in Indian cooking.

foods.name: Cinnamon
contraindications: high Pitta conditions in large amounts
foods.notes: Excellent for Kapha, traditionally used to support circulation and metabolism.

foods.name: Cloves
foods.notes: Very heating; classically used for respiratory/Kapha conditions and topically for toothache; not for large quantities.

foods.name: Tamarind
contraindications: high Pitta or acid reflux conditions
foods.notes: Some classical sources note tamarind can aggravate all three doshas in excess despite pacifying Vata in small quantity - guidance is mixed and quantity-dependent more than for most entries in this list.

foods.name: Walnuts
foods.notes: Traditionally recommended for Vata, particularly for nervous system support; best in moderation for Pitta and Kapha.

foods.name: Mustard Oil
foods.notes: Strongly heating; traditionally used more in colder regions/seasons and for Kapha conditions; generally avoided or minimized by Pitta-dominant individuals.
